old: worked hard for him — for the gods
new: worked hard for him—for the gods
reason: Edit 23 introduced the only spaced em dash in the Book; the binding rule (ODY-RULES, Book 10 lesson) is unspaced word—word, and Butler here has no dash at all ("who has worked hard for him, and whose labour the gods have prospered").

old: He would have given me something of my own by now:
new: He would have given me something of my own:
reason: Butler: "who would have been always good to me and given me something of my own"; the split sentence added by edit 23 supplies "by now", a time claim Butler does not make.

old: It was then that Zeus planned evil against me
new: It was then that Zeus devised evil against me
reason: Butler: "Then it was that Jove devised evil against me"; edit 14 chose "planned", which in this Book already renders Butler's different verb "counselled" ("when Zeus planned that terrible campaign" two sentences earlier, and ¶15 "Zeus planned their destruction"), so the listener hears an echo Butler does not have.

old: The men all fell into the sea and were carried about in the water around the ship,
new: The men all fell into the sea; they were carried about in the water round the ship,
reason: Butler's clause "they were carried about in the water round the ship" is word-for-word identical to B12-P35, which accepted Book 12 renders "The men all fell into the sea; they were carried about in the water round the ship, looking like so many seagulls"; ¶15 matches only the thunderbolt line and the "deprived" clause.

old: enough to support his family for ten generations, he had left so much of it in King Pheidon’s house.
new: enough to support his family for ten generations; that was how much he had left in King Pheidon’s house.
reason: Butler: "There was enough to keep his family for ten generations, so much had he left in the house of king Pheidon"; edit 27 un-inverted the clause but kept the comma, which leaves a comma splice in which "so much" reads as "a great deal" rather than Butler's "that much".
